title: Check yourself: how lambdas are built and what they may capture

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Per this page, how is a lambda expression compiled, compared with an anonymous inner class?

options.text: Into its own separate .class file, which javac writes out next to the enclosing one
options.says: The page says that is what happens to each anonymous class declaration, and that lambdas produce no separate class files at compile time.

options.text: Into a private copy of its body, placed at every spot in the code that calls it
options.says: The page names invokedynamic and a run-time generated implementing class; it describes no copying of the body into callers.

options.text: Through the invokedynamic instruction, with its implementing type generated at run time
options.says: The page's answer to Q2 says lambdas use invokedynamic and the implementing class is generated at run time.

questions.stem: Per this page, why may a lambda read a local variable of its method only when that variable is effectively final?

options.text: It receives a copy of the value, so a later change could never reach it
options.says: The page's answer to Q3 gives capture by value as the first reason: forbidding changes removes the confusion.

options.text: It runs on the thread that made it, before that method has returned
options.says: The page's answer to Q3 says a lambda might run in another thread, after the method that created it has returned.

options.text: It keeps a live link to the variable, so every change would reach it
options.says: The page's answer to Q3 says the lambda receives a copy of the value, so a later change could never be seen by it.

concepts: A lambda is compiled to an invokedynamic call and its class is made at run time, while each anonymous class gets its own class file.
A lambda may read a local variable only when it is final or effectively final, because it receives a copy of the value.
